items.note: Story 1: Association formed 1889, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891; Story 5 names Gideon Vose as founder.
Gives payment by butterfat test, not milk weight, but never says the test of the station where he delivers governs. Both bolded elements are required.
Only 'a critical decision that would shape the valley's history'. Never says that under payment by weight the fault would have cost nobody anything.
Loomis, Teague and Sill do not appear in Section A.
Names him as Gideon's son but says manager from 1911 (Stories 4 and 5). The key has 1913.
Section A never mentions the station-gain ledger line.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened May 4 1896. The borrowed Larrow Green glass is not in Section A, but the item has no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
Generic weigh/sample/test/separate outline. No composite sample, no fixed pipette charge, no percent read on the graduated neck.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, ordered April 14 1897, installed May 1 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, test bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Describes the deficit as '0.19–0.21' (Stories 3 and 8), not a flat 0.19 in every month of every year.
Never says a pipette could not be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Hired May 1896, dismissed April 30 1925, twenty-nine seasons.
The test book 'in his precise hand', meticulous records.
Section A gives 3.61 but not the 1896 figure of 3.80. Both are required.
Broke May 8 1911, nine weeks to July 10, tests up and then back down, question mark in the book. The 3.80 is missing but the item has no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
Wife Orra; 'Orra's brother Emmet, largest patron'.
Has the 1919 circular but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why.
Died February 1934, still under the accusation.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Weigh book mentioned only as an exhibit. No 1 Jan 1897 start, no agreement of the two scales.

Conflates the two gaps: G says Ostrey Hollow tested '0.19 points below valley average', and Section A gives the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.17–0.21 and '0.19–0.21 below the valley average'. The gate rule forfeits the item.
Says Grigg's committee 'spent the entire year of 1908 sampling'. The key has Jan–Mar only (F096, planted).
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss are not in Section A.
Custody of the weigh book (Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy 1958) is not in Section A.
Alder Corners is absent from Section A.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Rosalie Cudd is not in Section A.
Strawn 'conducted annual tests from 1908 onward'. The key has 1907 (NT-23).
Used the lactometer and found no added water at that station.
Condemned by Strawn on June 12 1923. The burette is not in Section A, but the item has no REQUIRED line, so the core fact carries it.
Never says he wrote no figure for the deficiency.
Section A says only 'when replaced in 1923, the tests immediately normalized'. No order dates, no 3.80 for 1924, no 'nobody connected it'. F1 separately asserts 3.85, which is deducted.
Crate in the loft is given, but not the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947. Both bolded elements are required.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Frick; March 17 – May 4 1925; three sittings, two in the weigh room.
The three theories appear (Story 4) but are never said to have been argued before the board and rejected. Theft is not attributed to Teague.
Four documents including Strawn's 1923 notebook, with Kyle's remark that nobody laid the second beside the fourth.
Dismissed April 30 1925 with no finding of dishonesty; $3,800 'without admission' on May 4. The account the award was charged to belongs to A7.6.
Section A gives the loss as $19,600, not $19,000, and never says the award was charged to the station-gain account.
Ivy Keddie, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Leland Vaught, Ansel's granddaughter.
No account of her assembling the separate record series.
Found in the loft in February 1958, but says eleven pipettes survived. The key has nine (NT-16).
Gives 16.27 cc, short 1.33 (NT-1).
Gives 92.44% of mark, not 95%. No 3.80 or 0.19 derivation.
Has 76,000 lb but $19,600. No 40,000,000 lb in Section A and no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 24 years after his death, 33 after the dismissal.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son (r18); r22's correction noted.
Second cousins, derived through Emmet and Orra being siblings and Roy and Duncan first cousins.
Never says whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings cannot be determined. Not asserted either way, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, son not nephew (Kyle).
Mentions Article 7 but gives the significance as the authority of the founding family. Does not say the father's rule made the faulty test decisive, nor the Vose-Jerseys largest-loser point.
Headline verdict: 'No established family relationship exists… not related by blood.' That is an assertion (−2 applied).
Treats Duncan's denial as settling the question. Does not say no document names or denies a link, nor that a family member's denial is not a record.
True average 3.90, short 0.29. Key: 3.80, 0.19.
Computes 116,000 lb. Mentions 76,000 only as the figure the sources cite.
Treats the 200,000 lb as the station total and gives 2,052–2,736 lb. Key: 6,840.
1,368,000 lb (subtracted instead of added). Key: 1,520,000.
Gives 5.26% of what was credited, correctly labelled, but omits the 5.00% of fat delivered. Both bolded elements are required.
72 pipettes is right, but short 1.33 cc, not 0.88. Both are required.
'26 years and 43 days', which is not an exact equivalent of 26 years 6 weeks (42 days). Also muddles the 25 full years into '≈26 full-year equivalents for financial calculation'.
Headline 'Approximately 1.1 million pounds' from Kyle's memory. That is an assertion (−2 applied).
Variable: the measuring glassware / pipettes; only the glass changed.
Held constant: tester, herds, procedure, acid, season, scales.
Result given as 'approximately 3.75–3.78'. Key: 3.80.
Rules out tester, milk and procedure, and states limits: does not show the pipettes deliver short, nor the mechanism.
The ledger reason is argued from the constancy of the percentage, not from the cream arriving heavy. Only two valid reasons (1911 interval, Strawn).
Argues the reasons are independent and names the 1911 interval as holding without 1958.
'No.' followed by Kyle's quote. That is an assertion (−2 applied).
Yes, he knew: 1902 complaints and the 1919 circular.
Only the 1919 circular among the five. Gives manager from 1911 (wrong), no ledger signatures, no 'nothing in his hand names the glass'.
'But did he know the glass was defective? No.' That is an assertion (−2 applied).

(1) Invoice $77.93 over $77.39, by the primary document. (2) Condemnation June 1923 over Kyle's 1922, first-hand inspector over clerk's memory. (3) Second cousins over Oram's 'first cousin once removed', by derivation (B2). None framed as a near-tie pair.

Award: explicitly says two narrators carry the same wrong $3,500 and breaks the tie with the chairman, records and clerk. It names r17 rather than the key's r01 as a carrier. NT-1 and NT-16 are resolved the wrong way (16.27; eleven).
A04 asserted (reground mold, accident). A06 and A10 not addressed as unsettleable.
Cites only r22's deliberate self-correction, which is not a narrator refuting itself on the page. None of the listed self-refutations identified.
Cause given as 16.27 cc / 7.56% short. Cessation given as a 1924 average of 3.85. No 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the 1911 interval.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same man at the bench.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214: five hundredths in winter, nothing in summer.
'No.' as the verdict on whether the board examined the glassware. That is an assertion (−2 applied).
'Ansel Keddie suspected it was something in the glass', taking the son's account as settled. That is an assertion (−2 applied).
Summary is about 176 words, over the 150 limit.
Fewer than five record series named (only the 1958 measurement clearly, and a vague 'state inspection').
Contains 16.27 and $19,600.
Only 1897, 1923 and 1958 present. One part in twenty wrong (16.27), money wrong ($19,600), Ansel and Ivy not named. Three of the six; four required.

Corruption: loss of $19,600 (F081), Story 8 and G
Corruption: eleven pipettes surviving (F089), Story 8 and E
Corruption: 1908 committee sampled the whole of 1908 (F096), Story 2
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911, Stories 4-5
Corruption: Strawn's circuit begun in 1908, Story 4 / D2 / F
Corruption: circular sent to eleven families (F058), Stories 4-5
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship asserted as 'not related' (B4)
Gullibility A02: 1896/first-season intake asserted as ~1.1 million lb (C5b)
Gullibility A03: asserts the manager did not know the tests were wrong (D3)
Gullibility A04: short lot asserted as an accident from a reground mold (Story 8, F1)
Gullibility A05: tester's belief asserted as 'something in the glass' (F)
Gullibility A07: board asserted not to have examined the glassware (F)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper asserted never to have questioned the entries (D2)
